extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political economy; policymakers and informed public interested in national wealth and public finance
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of classical political-economy principles about how capital, saving (parsimony), prodigality, public expenditure, and lending determine a nation's productive capacity and annual produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion between capital and revenue regulates industry and idleness
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion between capital and revenue, therefore, seems everywhere to regulate the proportion between industry and idleness. Wherever capital predominates, industry prevails; wherever revenue, idleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places where private capital predominates (funds employed to maintain productive labour) will tend to have more industry; places where revenue (public or passive income spent on consumption) predominates will tend toward idleness. Examples: comparison of Edinburgh (large public revenue spent) and Glasgow (inhabitants maintained by employment of capital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitals are increased by parsimony and diminished by prodigality and misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitals are increased by parsimony, and diminished by prodigality and misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saving (parsimony) adds to capital because what is saved from revenue becomes capital employed to maintain productive hands or lent for productive use. Prodigality and injudicious projects consume capital without reproducing its value, reducing funds for productive labour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsimony (saving) is the immediate cause of capital accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parsimony, and not industry, is the immediate cause of the increase of capital. Industry provides the subject which parsimony accumulates; but whatever industry might acquire, if parsimony did not save and store up, the capital would never be the greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While industry produces goods and value, accumulation of capital requires that part of that produce be saved rather than consumed. The saved portion becomes a perpetual fund maintaining productive labour over time; social incentives and private interest normally guard saved capital's productive use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between consumption by productive vs unproductive hands
rubrics_metrics.description: That portion of his revenue which a rich man annually spends ... is, in most cases, consumed by idle guests and menial servants, who leave nothing behind them in return for their consumption. That portion which he annually saves ... is consumed by labourers, manufacturers, and artificers, who reproduce, with a profit, the value of their annual consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumption that supports productive workers leads to reproduction of value (and thus sustains capital); consumption that supports unproductive or idle dependents does not reproduce value and thus reduces future productive capacity. The same amount of consumption can have very different effects depending on who is the consumer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prodigality perverts funds destined for productive labour
rubrics_metrics.description: The prodigal perverts it in this manner: By not confining his expense within his income, he encroaches upon his capital ... he pays the wages of idleness with those funds which the frugality of his forefathers had... consecrated to the maintenance of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extravagant spending that uses capital rather than income diminishes funds available for productive employment, reducing the annual produce and potentially impoverishing both the individual and, cumulatively, the country if widespread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct and unsuccessful projects diminish productive funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Every injudicious and unsuccessful project in agriculture, mines, fisheries, trade, or manufactures, tends in the same manner to diminish the funds destined for the maintenance of productive labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when capital is consumed by productive hands, injudicious application that fails to reproduce the full value of consumption reduces overall productive funds. This includes bad investments, failed enterprises, and imprudent undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public extravagance can impoverish a nation by maintaining unproductive hands
rubrics_metrics.description: Great nations are never impoverished by private, though they sometimes are by public prodigality and misconduct. The whole, or almost the whole public revenue is, in most countries, employed in maintaining unproductive hands... Such people, as they themselves produce nothing, are all maintained by the produce of other men's labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large public expenditures on courts, ecclesiastical establishments, standing fleets and armies (in peacetime) maintain unproductive persons and, if excessive and sustained, can force encroachment on capital and reduce future annual produce. The text gives historical examples (wars, debts) to illustrate the scale of such effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private frugality and good conduct generally offset individual and public waste
rubrics_metrics.description: The uniform, constant, and uninterrupted effort of every man to better his condition ... is frequently powerful enough to maintain the natural progress of things towards improvement, in spite both of the extravagance of government, and of the greatest errors of administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widespread private saving and prudent conduct tend to accumulate capital over time and can often compensate for private prodigality or even some degree of public extravagance, sustaining national improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual produce increases only via more productive labourers or higher productive powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual produce of the land and labour of any nation can be increased in its value by no other means, but by increasing either the number of its productive labourers, or the productive powers of those labourers who had before been employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing productivity requires either (a) more productive workers (which depends on greater capital/funds to maintain them) or (b) higher productivity per worker via better machines/instruments or improved division of labour — both pathways generally require additional capital investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money quantity follows value of annual produce (effect, not cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity of money, on the contrary, must in every country naturally increase as the value of the annual produce increases... The increase of those metals will, in this case, be the effect, not the cause, of the public prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount of circulating money needed is determined by the value of consumable goods circulated; increases in precious metals (money) accompany rising produce rather than causing it. Conversely, decline in produce can lead to outflow of money as holders seek employment for idle funds abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending on durable commodities is more favourable to accumulation than immediate consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The revenue of an individual may be spent, either in things which are consumed immediately ... or it may be spent in things more durable, which can therefore be accumulated... The one mode of expense is more favourable than the other to the opulence of an individual, so is it likewise to that of a nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenditure on durable goods (buildings, furniture, books, machinery, collections) tends to create accumulable assets that support future productive employment and diffusion of benefits to lower ranks, whereas lavish hospitality and immediately consumed entertainments often waste value and maintain unproductive hands. Durable spending also makes frugality easier to practice later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durable expenditure tends to maintain more productive employment than lavish hospitality
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense, besides, that is laid out in durable commodities, gives maintenance, commonly, to a greater number of people than that which is employed in the most profuse hospitality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durable investments typically employ masons, carpenters, upholsterers, mechanics, etc., distributing value across many productive workers and reducing waste compared to one-time feasts where a large share may be wasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock lent at interest is capital; productive use vs consumption determines sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: The stock which is lent at interest is always considered as a capital by the lender... The borrower may use it either as a capital, or as a stock reserved for immediate consumption. If he uses it as a capital, he employs it in the maintenance of productive labourers, who reproduce the value, with a profit... If he uses it as a stock reserved for immediate consumption, he acts the part of a prodigal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lenders expect restoration of the capital and interest. Lending for productive investment enables borrower to restore capital and pay interest; lending for consumption leads to encroachment on capital and is against the interest of both borrower and lender (except under usurious or exceptional conditions). Most loans are in money, but what matters is the money's worth (goods/services) and whether it is applied productively.
